title: Annual Owner's Meeting pushed one week
tldr: The virtual discussion has been moved back a week. A more detailed breakdown will be sent before the new date.
body_md:
The Annual Owner's Meeting is being pushed back **one week**.

A more detailed breakdown of every item below will go out before the new date. Open to other thoughts as well — drop anything you want to add by replying in Discord or posting a comment on the relevant Hall item.

Thanks for bearing with the reshuffle.

title: Website overall feedback
tldr: How is the league site / Hub working for you? What's broken, what's missing, what should we double down on?
body_md:
We've been pushing a lot of features to the league site this year (Contract Command Center, draft hub, MCM, rookies hub, etc.).

## What I want from you

- **What's working** — the views or features you actually open more than once.
- **What's broken** — anything that's confusing, slow, or wrong.
- **What's missing** — what would make you visit weekly instead of monthly.

Drop a 👍 / 👎 / 🤷 for general read, then leave a comment with the specifics. This isn't a vote — it's input that drives what I prioritize next.

title: Superflex — Year 1 retro with relaxed rules
tldr: Did the year-one tweaks (3 starting QBs by deadline, max 5 QB active roster) work, or do they need adjustment?
body_md:
Year 1 of Superflex shipped with relaxed rules:

- **3 starting QBs required** by the tag deadline
- **Max 5 QBs** on the active roster

## What I want to know

- Did the added flexibility actually help your roster construction?
- Did the cap of 5 active QBs ever bite you?
- Did the 3-QB minimum feel like the right floor, or do we need more / less?

This is sentiment + comments only — feeds into a possible **formal vote** for Year 2 changes (which would be its own Hall item).

title: Realignment — captain-based division draft
tldr: Replace formula-based division alignment with a captain-based draft. All-Play % picks 4 captains; captains snake-draft their division mates. Realignment runs every 3 years.
body_md:
**The change**

All-Play % no longer picks divisions — it picks **Division Captains** only. Captains snake-draft their division mates.

**Format**
- **Top 4 teams by All-Play %** become Division Captains
- **Snake draft, 2 rounds:** Round 1 picks 1→4, Round 2 picks 4→1
- Divisions are no longer formula-generated
- **The snake draft happens at the Rookie Draft every 3 years** — when everyone is present. Yes, that means the last-picked dodgeball kid (the #1 pick) gets ridiculed in person. Adds an excellent layer of league entertainment.

**Seeding**
- **2026 (this realignment):** full historical All-Play %
- **Going forward (every 3 years):** rolling 3-year All-Play %
- **Captain eligibility:** owners must have been in the league the full 3-year prior window to be eligible for Captain

**Why**
- Current formula produces repeat clustering — same teams keep landing in the same divisions cycle after cycle
- **Of 66 possible current-owner pairings, only 29 have ever shared a division — 37 pairs have never been divisional opponents-of-record across the 5 realignment cycles since 2011**
- Some pairs have shared 15 seasons of league time without ever once landing in the same division
- Captain draft creates more variety — and more fun

**The vote**
- ✅ **YES** — adopt captain-based draft + rolling 3-yr All-Play
- ❌ **NO** — keep current formula-based assignment
- ➖ **ABSTAIN** — recorded but doesn't decide

title: Tagging — early lock-in becomes a tradeable asset
tldr: Allow owners to lock in their tag selection early. Once locked, it becomes a tradeable asset and is final.
body_md:
*Note: this rule is **most relevant for next year** — we're already at the tag lock deadline this season, so the early-lock-in mechanic effectively kicks in for the 2027 cycle.*

**The change**

Allow owners to **lock in** their tag selection early. Today, applying a tag does not lock the player — they auto-lock on tag deadline day. This proposal adds an explicit "Lock in" action: once a tagged player is locked in, the tag is final and the asset is tradeable.

Once locked:
- The tag becomes a **tradeable asset** — packageable in trades like any other contract
- The selection is **final** — no take-backs, no swaps to a different player after lock-in

**Why**
- Adds a real strategic lever — owners who know early which player they want to retain can use the tag itself as a trade chip

**Risk / what to watch**
- A tag locked early can't be undone if the player suffers a season-ending injury before the deadline
- *Mitigation:* the player can still be dropped cap-penalty-free up until the deadline

**Trade mechanics (clarified)**
- The receiving team acquires the player **and** the contract
- The tag does **not** count against the receiving team's tag totals — they retain full control over their own tags

**The vote**
- ✅ **YES** — adopt early lock-in + tradeable tag
- ❌ **NO** — keep tags as deadline-only, non-tradeable
- ➖ **ABSTAIN** — recorded but doesn't decide

title: Salary depreciation — move to true pro-rated model
tldr: Replace the current step-based depreciation with a true pro-rated model that earns salary by completed week of eligibility.
body_md:
**Current model**
- *Non-WW Players:* 25% earned by end of Oct · 50% by end of Nov · 75% by end of Dec · 100% by season end
- *Waiver wire (WW):* flat 35% regardless of pickup date

**Proposed — true pro-rated**

*Non-WW Players (Auction + Week-1 acquisitions):* earned per completed week.
- After Week 1 → 1/17 earned · Week 2 → 2/17 · Week 3 → 3/17 · …through full season

*Mid-season pickups:* pro-rated over remaining eligible weeks.
- Example A — picked up in Week 9 (**9 weeks remaining**: Weeks 9–17): Week 9 → 1/9 · Week 10 → 2/9 · …
- Example B — picked up in Week 7 (**11 weeks remaining**: Weeks 7–17): Week 7 → 1/11 · Week 8 → 2/11 · …

*WW pickups under this model* — treated identically to auction contracts: same **75% guarantee**, same earning math, same cap-penalty timing. The only difference is the window — WW pickups have fewer weeks remaining to earn.

**Why now**
- Available data makes this easy to track and maintain
- Better reflects how real contracts accrue value over time
- Can be applied immediately — offseason timing allows a clean transition across all teams

**What changes for owners**
- Total cap hit over a contract's life is **unchanged**
- Only the *timing* of when salary is earned changes

**What does NOT change** *(current rules carry forward)*
- WW pickups **under $4K** remain cap-penalty-free if dropped
- Multi-year contracts where TCV < $5K still carry the **fixed $1K penalty** if dropped with more than 1 year remaining
- All cap penalties are **rounded based on the SUM of penalties accrued**, not per-penalty

**The vote**
- ✅ **YES** — adopt true pro-rated depreciation (replaces both auction curve and WW)
- ❌ **NO** — keep the current model (auction step-function + flat 35% WW)
- ➖ **ABSTAIN** — recorded but doesn't decide

title: Taxi squad flexibility — temporary call-ups before permanent move
tldr: Owners can temporarily call up a taxi player up to 3 weeks across their 3-year taxi window before the move becomes permanent.
body_md:
**The change**

Owners can call up a taxi player to the active roster temporarily — up to **3 weeks total per player** across their taxi-eligible window (their first 3 years in the league). After that, the call-up becomes permanent. All standard taxi eligibility rules still apply.

**How it works**
- Each call-up is a one-week commitment. Player counts against active roster limits **and** salary cap for that NFL week.
- After the week, the owner can return the player to the taxi squad.
- Each active week counts as **1** toward the player's 3-week limit. Weeks are cumulative across seasons — consecutive or non-consecutive both count.
- On the **4th week** of activation, the call-up becomes **permanent**.

**Why**
- We now have the tracking in place to manage this with minimal manual work
- Lets owners use taxi players in short-term roles without permanently committing
- Removes the current "one-week activation = permanent loss" trap
- Mirrors how NFL teams use practice squad elevations
- Introduces strategy while keeping accountability — every activation burns a finite allowance

**The vote**
- ✅ **YES** — adopt temporary call-ups with the 3-week limit per player
- ❌ **NO** — keep the current taxi rule (permanent call-up only)
- ➖ **ABSTAIN** — recorded but doesn't decide

*Behind the scenes: every owner's call-up usage will be tracked and visible so eligibility is auditable.*

title: Dynasty Pot — +$50 annual dues, 3-year prize
tldr: Add $50 to annual dues to fund a 3-year Dynasty Pot — annual prize boost plus a larger cumulative prize at the end of each 3-year cycle.
body_md:
**The change**

Add **$50 to annual dues** to fund a 3-year Dynasty Pot — annual prize boost + a larger cumulative prize at end of each 3-year cycle. Coincides with the divisional realignment cycle, so each Dynasty Pot tracks the same 3-year window as captaincy seeding.

**Pot math**
- 12 teams × $50 × 3 years = **$1,800** per cycle
- **$900** — 3-Year Dynasty Prize: best 3-year All-Play % at end of cycle
- **$900** — annual payouts: $300/yr (suggested **$200 → 1st · $100 → 2nd**, open to alternatives)

**Eligibility**
- Owners must be in the league all 3 years to be eligible
- Owners who leave forfeit all contributions — no reimbursement
- New owners pay the $50 upon joining but aren't eligible until they complete a full 3-year cycle
- **All-Play %** is the deciding factor
- **Prize splitting** is only allowed in the event of a tie — voluntary splits aren't recognized

**Why**
- Rewards sustained dynasty success, not just single-season performance
- Longer-term incentive for every team, including rebuilds — you don't need to win a title, just perform best over 3 years
- Given the time + effort owners pour in, **$50/yr is a small investment** for a meaningful prize

**Historical 3-year cycle AP% leaders** *(informal — never paid out)*
- 2011–2013: Derrick Whitman (70.5%)
- 2014–2016: Ryan Bousquet (70.2%)
- 2017–2019: Josh Martel (73.8%)
- 2020–2022: Steve Bousquet (67.6%)
- 2023–2025: Ryan Bousquet (64.9%)

**Approval threshold**
Dues change — **requires 75% approval (9 of 12 YES)** to pass.

**The vote**
- ✅ **YES** — fund the Dynasty Pot
- ❌ **NO** — keep dues unchanged
- ➖ **ABSTAIN** — recorded but doesn't decide

title: MYM — restrict eligibility on late-season drops
tldr: Direction-setting vote: should players dropped from December 1st onward (in the final year of their deal) become ineligible for MYM acquisition?
body_md:
**Direction-setting vote** — gauging whether the league wants to pursue this rule.

**The end-of-season problem**

In December, contracts in their final year carry **no cap penalty** to drop. Teams can release known stars who are temporarily devalued (injured, slumping) — and other teams can grab them via MYM at a steeply discounted value.

*Real example — 2025:* CMC injured on IR taking ~50% of cap. Owner held him to avoid handing the league a discounted MYM opportunity. But other owners wouldn't necessarily do the same. As commish, my bias toward league integrity becomes a competitive disadvantage.

**The conflict**
- Competitive fairness vs. individual roster flexibility
- MYM was designed for waiver-wire value discovery — not for acquiring established stars at discounted rates

**Potential direction**
A player becomes **ineligible for MYM** if ALL of the following are true:
1. They were under contract at the **contract deadline date**
2. They were on a roster **all season** (never dropped or traded out earlier)
3. They were dropped **in December**

The restriction lasts the remainder of the season.

*Note: this is separate from the existing 1-week-wait rule (a player dropped, then re-acquired, must wait one week before being offered as MYM). That rule is unchanged here — different problem.*

**The vote**
- ✅ **YES** — pursue this direction; draft a formal rule
- ❌ **NO** — keep the current rule
- ➖ **ABSTAIN** — recorded but doesn't decide

*If you have a better mechanism, drop it in the reasoning when you vote.*
